newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: U.S. AGENCY GRANTS ZAMBIA $7 MLN IN NEW AID.
newsitem.headline: U.S. AGENCY GRANTS ZAMBIA $7 MLN IN NEW AID.

text.p: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) on Tuesday committed $7 million towards four existing development projects in Zambia, effectively lifting a freeze on aid to the country.

The United States was among Western governments which tightened aid flows to Zambia last year in protest against constitutional changes enforced by the Frederick Chiluba government before general elections last November.
Seven political parties boycotted the polls, later won by Chiluba's Movement for Multiparty Democracy.

U.S. Ambassador Arlene Render and Zambian Finance Minister Ronald Penza signed agreements for the fresh aid, targeted at agricultural sector liberalisation, privatisation, family planning and child health care in the capital Lusaka.

At a donor meeting on Zambia earlier in July, donors said they would ease restrictions on aid flows to the southern African country, satisfied with the government's economic reforms, including its privatisation programme.
Render said the Zambia privatisation support projects was a six-year $20 million programme which began in 1992 to support privatisation.
"The current additional $2 million completes funding of the project," Render told reporters at the signing ceremony.

The ambassador said the agricultural liberalisation project was a five-year programme worth $23 million which began in 1994, aimed at increasing the ability of rural farmers to participate in the market economy.
With the new funding of $1.2 million to the programme, USAID will have contributed $8.2 million to the project.
The five-year $20 million family planning services project from 1993 is being boosted by an additional $1.8 million.
Render said the Zambia child health care project over five years, worth $20 million, was designed to increase the coverage and quality of activities in child health care.
"The current funding provides $2 million, bringing the amount funded to date to $7.5 million," she said.
The Zambian government has said it needs $200 million in balance of payments support and about $275 million in project financing in 1997.
